39:11.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّيٓ أُمِرۡتُ أَنۡ أَعۡبُدَ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصࣰ ا لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ
39:11.en: Say (O Muhammad): Lo! I am commanded to worship Allah, making religion pure for Him (only)

39:12.en: And I am commanded to be the first of those who are muslims (surrender unto Him)

39:13.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ إِنۡ عَصَيۡتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
39:13.en: Say: Lo! if I should disobey my Lord, I fear the doom of a tremendous Day

39:14.ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهَ أَعۡبُدُ مُخۡلِصࣰ ا لَّهُۥ دِينِي
39:14.en: Say: Allah I worship, making my religion pure for Him (only)

39:15.ar: فَٱعۡبُدُواْ مَا شِئۡتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦۗ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَهۡلِيهِمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ أَلَا ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخُسۡرَانُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
39:15.en: Then worship what ye will beside Him. Say: The losers will be those who lose themselves and their housefolk on the Day of Resurrection. Ah, that will be the manifest loss

39:16.ar: لَهُم مِّن فَوۡقِهِمۡ ظُلَلࣱ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ وَمِن تَحۡتِهِمۡ ظُلَلࣱۚ ذَٰلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦ عِبَادَهُۥۚ يَٰعِبَادِ فَٱتَّقُونِ
39:16.en: They have an awning of fire above them and beneath them a dais (of fire). With this doth Allah appal His bondmen. O My bondmen, therefor fear Me

39:17.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱجۡتَنَبُواْ ٱلطَّٰغُوتَ أَن يَعۡبُدُوهَا وَأَنَابُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ لَهُمُ ٱلۡبُشۡرَىٰۚ فَبَشِّرۡ عِبَادِ
39:17.en: And those who put away false gods lest they should worship them and turn to Allah in repentance, for them there are glad tidings. Therefor give good tidings (O Muhammad) to My bondmen

39:18.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحۡسَنَهُۥٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
39:18.en: Who hear advice and follow the best thereof. Such are those whom Allah guideth, and such are men of understanding

17:1.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَسۡرَىٰ بِعَبۡدِهِۦ لَيۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡأَقۡصَا ٱلَّذِي بَٰرَكۡنَا حَوۡلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَآۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
17:1.en: Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship the neighbourhood whereof We have blessed, that We might show him of Our tokens! Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Seer

39:5.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ يُكَوِّرُ ٱلَّيۡلَ عَلَى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ ٱلنَّهَارَ عَلَى ٱلَّيۡلِۖ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِي لِأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمًّىۗ أَلَا هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفَّٰرُ
39:5.en: He hath created the heavens and the earth with truth. He maketh night to succeed day, and He maketh day to succeed night, and He constraineth the sun and the moon to give service, each running on for an appointed term. Is not He the Mighty, the Forgiver

39:6.ar: خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسࣲ وَٰحِدَةࣲ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنۡهَا زَوۡجَهَا وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ ثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَزۡوَٰجࣲۚ يَخۡلُقُكُمۡ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡ خَلۡقࣰ ا مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَلۡقࣲ فِي ظُلُمَٰتࣲ ثَلَٰثࣲۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصۡرَفُونَ
39:6.en: He created you from one being, then from that (being) He made its mate; and He hath provided for you of cattle eight kinds. He created you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in a threefold gloom. Such is Allah, your Lord. His is the Sovereignty. There is no Allah save Him. How then are ye turned away

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the endeavour which is His right. He hath chosen you and hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship; the faith of your father Abraham (is yours). He hath named you Muslims of old time and in this (Scripture), that the messenger may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against mankind. So establish worship, pay the poor-due, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protecting friend. A blessed Patron and a blessed Helper

23:60.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡتُونَ مَآ ءَاتَواْ وَّقُلُوبُهُمۡ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ رَٰجِعُونَ
23:60.en: And those who give that which they give with hearts afraid because they are about to return unto their Lord

70:27.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنۡ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشۡفِقُونَ
70:27.en: And those who are fearful of their Lord's doom

70:28.en: Lo! the doom of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure

12:87.ar: يَٰبَنِيَّ ٱذۡهَبُواْ فَتَحَسَّسُواْ مِن يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَاْيۡـَٔسُواْ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَاْيۡـَٔسُ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
12:87.en: Go, O my sons, and ascertain concerning Joseph and his brother, and despair not of the Spirit of Allah. Lo! none despaireth of the Spirit of Allah save disbelieving folk

7:169.ar: فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفࣱ وَرِثُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يَأۡخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغۡفَرُ لَنَا وَإِن يَأۡتِهِمۡ عَرَضࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥ يَأۡخُذُوهُۚ أَلَمۡ يُؤۡخَذۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّيثَٰقُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَن لَّا يَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّ وَدَرَسُواْ مَا فِيهِۗ وَٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
7:169.en: And a generation hath succeeded them who inherited the scriptures. They grasp the goods of this low life (as the price of evil-doing) and say: It will be forgiven us. And if there came to them (again) the offer of the like, they would accept it (and would sin again). Hath not the covenant of the Scripture been taken on their behalf that they should not speak aught concerning Allah save the truth? And they have studied that which is therein. And the abode of the Hereafter is better, for those who ward off (evil). Have ye then no sense

89:27.en: But ah! thou soul at peace

89:28.en: Return unto thy Lord, content in His good pleasure

7:171.ar: ۞وَإِذۡ نَتَقۡنَا ٱلۡجَبَلَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُۥ ظُلَّةࣱ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُۥ وَاقِعُۢ بِهِمۡ خُذُواْ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةࣲ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
7:171.en: And when We shook the Mount above them as it were a covering, and they supposed that it was going to fall upon them (and We said): Hold fast that which We have given you, and remember that which is therein, that ye may ward off (evil)

39:55.ar: وَٱتَّبِعُوٓاْ أَحۡسَنَ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ بَغۡتَةࣰ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَشۡعُرُونَ
39:55.en: And follow the better (guidance) of that which is revealed unto you from your Lord, before the doom cometh on you suddenly when ye know not

5:27.ar: ۞وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱبۡنَيۡ ءَادَمَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ إِذۡ قَرَّبَا قُرۡبَانࣰ ا فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنۡ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمۡ يُتَقَبَّلۡ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓخَرِ قَالَ لَأَقۡتُلَنَّكَۖ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
5:27.en: But recite unto them with truth the tale of the two sons of Adam, how they offered each a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the one of them and it was not accepted from the other. (The one) said: I will surely kill thee. (The other) answered: Allah accepteth only from those who ward off (evil)

kkttkvfI3gc.speaker: adnan
kkttkvfI3gc.speaker_note: continues his weekly Arabic tafsir of Az-Zumar from verse 11, answering a congregant's point mid-lesson
kkttkvfI3gc.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Az-Zumar (39:11-18)
kkttkvfI3gc.one_line: Worship as loving service, being first among Muslims in sincerity, fear without despair, losing oneself on the Last Day, and following the best of what you hear.
kkttkvfI3gc.summary: Sincerity is the greatest act of the heart and the inner basis of tawhid; without it there is no Islam. Verse 11 commands worshipping Allah with religion sincerely His, which requires understanding worship: it means service, and since Allah needs nothing, we serve Him by serving His creation, starting with parents and family; linguistically 'ubudiyyah is also among the highest degrees of love, a self levelled like a paved road so nothing He commands hurts. Being 'first of the Muslims' means first in quality, not time. The Prophet is told to say he fears the punishment of a great Day if he disobeys; this fear is the first step on the path, not a reason for despair, and the righteous all died afraid while Muslims today feel strangely secure. 'Allah alone I worship, sincere in my religion' adds one's personal choices to the general religion. The true losers lose themselves and their families on the Last Day: the self is utterly devoted to you but ignorant of what is good, so it must be educated. Those who avoid false gods and turn back to Allah are given good news: they listen to speech and follow the best of it, choosing the way of applying a command that is most sincere and most effective, as Hasan and Husayn taught an old man to make wudu.

outline.heading: Acts of the heart outweigh acts of the limbs
outline.gist: Limb worship without the heart is empty; Allah asks about our hearts as He asks about our wudu.

outline.heading: Sincerity is the greatest act of the heart, and a gift
outline.gist: Every believer seeks it; we walk its path, but Allah grants it, and emptying the heart of all but Him is a high rank.

outline.heading: Without sincerity there is no tawhid
outline.gist: Tawhid is the outward core of Islam and sincerity its inward basis, opposed by showing off; here mind and heart meet.

outline.heading: Verses 11-14 recited: merging without nasal sound
outline.gist: The repetition of sincerity leaves no doubt about the surah's axis.

outline.heading: Worship is not only rituals
outline.gist: Limiting worship to rituals wrongs the word; at root it means service.

outline.heading: Serving the One who needs nothing
outline.gist: Allah needs nothing, so serving Him means serving His servants: parents, spouse, children, society, the ummah, humanity and all creatures.

outline.heading: Servanthood is the highest honour
outline.gist: A servant does not seek rank; the Prophet is praised as 'His servant', and every choice should show you are Allah's servant.

outline.heading: The worth of servitude follows the One served
outline.gist: Serving the Lord of the heavens is the highest station; serving the world lowers you to its level.

outline.heading: Everyone is a slave to something; 'ubudiyyah as love
outline.gist: Al-Tha'alibi ranks 'ubudiyyah among the highest stages of love; a paved road feels nothing when walked on.

outline.heading: Service mixed with love and no objection
outline.gist: Accept whatever He commands, easy or hard; only Allah can confirm that you truly reached servitude.

outline.heading: Sincerity makes servitude real
outline.gist: Servitude with rivals in the heart is full of bumps; the Prophet was commanded directly, as Iblis was and refused.

outline.heading: Even if no one else on earth obeyed
outline.gist: Fast, lower your gaze and eat halal only for Him, not for people or your conscience.

outline.heading: First of the Muslims: first in quality
outline.gist: Ibrahim and Adam came before him, so it means the best in practice; this is where people compete.

outline.heading: Two sincere men: 'from Allah, not from you'
outline.gist: The giver gives for Allah and the receiver takes from Allah; the sincere deal with Allah through people.

outline.heading: I fear the punishment of a great Day
outline.gist: The Prophet himself is told to say he fears disobeying in the matter of sincerity.

outline.heading: Fear is the first step, not despair
outline.gist: Sincerity is a path, not a station you reach; feeling afraid for your deeds means you have stepped onto it.

outline.heading: Muslims who are sure of Paradise
outline.gist: No prophet or righteous person died feeling secure; imitate the salaf in their fear before their dress.

outline.heading: Fear without despair, and keep reckoning
outline.gist: Never lose hope in Allah's mercy, but keep checking your intentions and correcting them.

outline.heading: 'Allah alone I worship': your personal religion
outline.gist: 'The religion' is what Allah commanded all; 'my religion' covers one's own choices; putting Allah's name first restricts worship to Him.

outline.heading: Verses 15-18 recited; 'worship what you will' as rebuke
outline.gist: The command is sarcastic, meaning nothing besides Him will benefit you.

outline.heading: The human love of winning
outline.gist: Like a child who must win every game, this drive helps when used in obedience.

outline.heading: Losing yourself and your family
outline.gist: Either he led his family into the Fire or they went to Paradise and he will never see them again.

outline.heading: The self is devoted to you but ignorant
outline.gist: The self wants only your good but thinks it is wealth and power; it must be taught like a child.

outline.heading: Worldly victories mean nothing if you lose yourself
outline.gist: The self can become tranquil; your trophies will not help you on the Last Day.

outline.heading: Canopies of fire above and below
outline.gist: Allah warns His servants of this so they protect themselves now.

outline.heading: Avoiding taghut, continuously
outline.gist: Taghut is anything worshipped besides Allah; the verb form allows one who slipped once and repented to be included.

outline.heading: Following the best of what they hear
outline.gist: All Allah's speech is good; 'the best' refers to choosing the most sincere and effective way to apply a command.

outline.heading: Hasan, Husayn and the old man's wudu
outline.gist: Instead of correcting him they asked him to judge their wudu, and he realized his own mistake.

outline.heading: Habil and Qabil: giving the best you have
outline.gist: One offered his best and one his worst; in moral matters only you know whether you gave your best.

outline.heading: The truth can be carried in many ships
outline.gist: Harshness is not 'speaking the truth'; those who follow the best are the guided, the people of understanding.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them

arv4d_6u6Ac.title: Five Additional Points to Consider During Difficult Times
arv4d_6u6Ac.one_line: During the Gaza war he offers five points: it is a wake-up call, long-term work matters most, advocate long-term, invest in youth, and don't let anger rule you.
arv4d_6u6Ac.summary: Struggling to keep a straight face after three Gaza hospitals were bombed, and noting that Afghanistan's earthquake has been all but ignored, he offers five points to reflect on. First, why this is happening: harsh wake-up calls come to a generation cruising through comfortable, trivial lives, and dark moments are when people find their calling, so the suffering must not be wasted by going back to normal in a few months. Second, short-term efforts such as emails, rallies, calls, boycotts and following local advocacy groups are everyone's duty, but what is reaped today was sown thirty years ago, so the unglamorous long-term work, like an elder quietly teaching children in a masjid corner, decides the future. The Prophet himself died before seeing Islam spread across continents. Third, long-term advocacy: for every child killed there, a child here should be educated to speak on their behalf, because the ummah is one family. Fourth, youth are the source of hope and must be protected and equipped in schools and universities so they never feel they must hide their identity, as the hadith of planting a sapling at the Hour teaches. Fifth, oppression wrapped in lies provokes anger, but a single rogue word can become the whole story, so be wise and consult.

outline.heading: Opening
Hospitals bombed, an earthquake ignored
outline.gist: It is hard to function while the death toll climbs; three hospitals were just hit, the world twiddles its thumbs, and Afghanistan's earthquake goes almost unnoticed.

outline.heading: Point one: harsh wake-up calls
outline.gist: Why this is happening, in the philosophical sense: a generation asleep at the wheel or lost in trivial bubbles gets a harsh wake-up call, and in the darkest moments people find their calling, as Western Muslims losing jobs and status are doing.

outline.heading: A chance to change your life
outline.gist: Wake-up calls come to people cruising through comfortable plans; whether you are 15 or 85, this is an opportunity to make hard, meaningful decisions and walk a path with purpose.

outline.heading: May their suffering not be in vain
outline.gist: His fear is that in two or three months this becomes a distant memory and everyone returns to trivial concerns.

outline.heading: Point two: the short-term work
outline.gist: Emails, rallies, calls, social media, boycotts and following local advocacy groups such as Hikma or NCCM are everyone's duty while pushing for a ceasefire, but the long-term plan makes the difference.

outline.heading: What we reap today was sown thirty years ago
outline.gist: Today's reality was set in motion long ago; whatever we sow now decides whether the next generation faces the same problem.

outline.heading: Long-term work is boring: the elder in the corner
outline.gist: Long-term work is unattractive and makes no news; change comes from the older man or woman quietly teaching a few children in a corner of the masjid.

outline.heading: The Prophet never saw the fruits
outline.gist: Volunteers flood in during a crisis and vanish after it; the Prophet died when Islam covered parts of Arabia, and only thirty years later under Uthman did it span continents, yet he was content to do his part.

outline.heading: Point three: a voice here for every life taken there
outline.gist: For every child, woman, man or elder buried under the rubble, someone here will be educated to speak for them, because the ummah is one family.

outline.heading: Control what you can
outline.gist: We cannot stop the bombs, but we can educate and prepare those who will be their voice and move the needle; that is long-term advocacy.

outline.heading: Point four: the youth are where hope is
outline.gist: A natural pessimist, he finds hope only in working with youth; they must be protected and advocated for in schools and universities, never left where they are targeted.

outline.heading: Plant the sapling as the Hour comes
outline.gist: The hadith shows the Islamic mentality of hope: do your part without deciding whether it will bear fruit; young people being targeted must never feel they have to hide their identity.

outline.heading: Point five: oppression wrapped in lies provokes anger
outline.gist: Taking what is not yours is one thing; making the oppressed look evil while denying it goes one step too far and naturally provokes anger.

outline.heading: Do not let anger dictate: one wrong word becomes the story
outline.gist: One Muslim saying one wrong thing would eclipse 3,372 dead children; work as a group, keep speaking the truth wisely, and consult those with more knowledge.

outline.heading: Outro

Qsy0Gj-MXSA.title: The Solution Is from Within
Qsy0Gj-MXSA.one_line: Thirty-three days into the Gaza bombardment, he argues from hadith and Surat An-Nur that the ummah's weakness and its revival both come from within.
Qsy0Gj-MXSA.summary: He opens with the Al-Anfal warning that disputes make believers fail and lose their strength, then turns to Gaza: 33 days of bombardment on a strip smaller than London, 11,000 dead including 4,000 children. He expected nothing from the West but is baffled by the weak response of Muslim countries, and sarcastically thanks the Canadian government for ending the illusion that Muslims' voices and blood count equally. The real lesson, he says, is that Muslims only have each other. He narrates the hadith in which the Prophet asked that his ummah not be destroyed by a general calamity or an outside enemy, and Allah granted both, except that they would destroy one another. Surat An-Nur's promise of stewardship, security and an established faith holds for believers who worship Allah alone and do good, so if it is not fulfilled the failure is ours. The only thing a believer may complain about is his own effort; self-pity and blame are not allowed. In the second khutbah he reminds them the ummah has survived worse, which proves recovery is possible, not guaranteed. He finds this empowering: our destiny is still in our hands. There is collective as well as individual accountability, so Muslims must live for something bigger than houses and comfort, as servants of Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Do not dispute or your strength departs
outline.gist: The Al-Anfal command to obey Allah and the Prophet and not divide, or believers fail and their "wind", their momentum and chance of prevailing, is gone.

outline.heading: Gaza after 33 days
outline.gist: A strip smaller than London has been bombarded for 33 days, its people pushed into denser places; 11,000 dead including 4,000 children, four times the children he has served in his whole life. He never expected anything from the West.

outline.heading: A thank-you to his government: we only have each other
outline.gist: Muslim countries' advocacy fails to move the needle; he sarcastically thanks his government for ending the illusion that Muslims' voices, principles and blood carry equal value, and for the lesson that our strength, like our weakness, comes from within.

outline.heading: The Prophet's request: never destroyed from outside
outline.gist: Shown the east and west his ummah would reach and its treasures, he asked that it not perish by a general calamity like earlier nations or by an outside enemy; Allah granted both, except that they would destroy one another.

outline.heading: Never an external problem
outline.gist: This was the Prophet's lifelong teaching and the Quran's: we waste time on outside powers, but it is weakness within that lets this happen and strength within that will change the future.

outline.heading: A promise for this world
outline.gist: Most Quranic promises concern the hereafter; there is one for individuals, a few for groups, and this verse of An-Nur is one of the few made to the nation itself.

outline.heading: The terms of the promise
outline.gist: Stewardship of the earth, an established faith and security in place of fear, as long as they worship Allah alone; keep up prayer and every obligation and obey the Prophet, and do not think the enemy beyond Allah's reach.

outline.heading: The only permitted complaint: your own effort
outline.gist: Allah made a promise, so if it has not come through we did not fulfil our part of the deal; that is all we may complain about.

outline.heading: Bring back self-accountability
outline.gist: The unfulfilled promise is the doing of our own hands; self-criticism and self-awareness must return to individuals and communities. He hates this reality, but who is there to blame?

outline.heading: No self-pity, whatever you have been through
outline.gist: However often you have been removed or oppressed, this is not the time to feel sorry for yourself; hold yourself accountable and commit long-term, in unity, and the light will appear.

outline.heading: Interlude
We have been through worse
outline.gist: The ummah survived darker times when it was weaker, more divided and smaller, preserving its faith, book and language; that proves it can recover, not that it will.

outline.heading: Success comes through the people in this room
outline.gist: Victory will come through the commitment of the individuals before him, turning their lives around, dropping worthless distractions and staying on the path whether or not brothers are falling.

outline.heading: Our destiny is still in our hands
outline.gist: Being destroyed only from within is empowering: no outsider ever controlled our fate; our advocacy, work, unity and sincerity decide it.

outline.heading: "It was never my business"
outline.gist: He wishes he could tell Allah he was only keeping food on the table, but it turns out he contributes, and so does everyone.

outline.heading: Collective accountability
outline.gist: Besides individual judgment, a generation is held to account for neglected collective obligations, including those who stayed on the outside looking after themselves.

outline.heading: Live for something bigger
outline.gist: These events should revive activism and living for Allah rather than for a house and settled children; a servant of Allah was designed for more.

outline.heading: Solution and demise both come from within
outline.gist: Life is not a walk in the park avoiding controversy; these events remind us of the truth, and Allah's promise is that the ummah prevails or fails from within.

outline.heading: Outro

NX3u40_iNJc.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 7: Verses 22-24 (The Names of Allah)
NX3u40_iNJc.one_line: The closing names of Al-Hashr: why tawhid anchors constant values, and what each name from al-Alim to al-Musawwir teaches about Allah.
NX3u40_iNJc.summary: He explains why a juz of rulings is punctuated by verses on Allah: without the ihsan dimension of why and for whom, practice loses its spirit, becomes harsh and even harmful, as fasting turned into nightly overeating shows, and Muslims who share fundamentals end up dividing over approaches. The closing verses hold the densest run of divine names in the Quran. Huwa carries no gender. 'No god but He' puts negation first, and he argues only the Quranic description of God is philosophically coherent, recalling his shock at a visiting priest's description of God. Tawhid matters because it is the only constant source of values; self-made or committee-made boundaries keep moving, while a Muslim's values stay fixed anywhere in time, so a sinner who knows the sin is wrong is still reachable. Knower of the unseen and seen means science can never prove God, who is outside the measurable world. He then walks through al-Rahman and al-Rahim, al-Malik who owns us yet grants rights by grace, al-Quddus, al-Salam, al-Mu'min, al-Muhaymin, al-Aziz, al-Jabbar who compels and mends, and al-Mutakabbir, where human arrogance is being out of place and humility is seeing reality. Creating from nothing, giving life and giving it its drive are three questions science will never answer.

outline.heading: The densest cluster of Allah's names
outline.gist: No other passage lists so many names in sequence; learning the names is how we know Allah, our deen and ourselves.

outline.heading: Why a technical juz pauses for the heart
outline.gist: Amid rulings on relationships, every second surah has moving verses so we do not forget why we act.

outline.heading: Islam, iman and the neglected ihsan
outline.gist: Without knowing why and for whom we act, practice drifts into my group against yours.

outline.heading: Divided over approach, not goals
outline.gist: Most Muslims agree on values and differ only on routes, which should never cause division.

outline.heading: The same act done with or without spirit
outline.gist: Truth can be said mercifully or harshly, prayer done with presence or without; the missing layer later corrupts the act.

outline.heading: Ramadan turned into overeating
outline.gist: Fasting is a huge ask against every living thing's instinct; forgetting why turns it into an inconvenience and a health hazard.

outline.heading: Actions are by intentions
outline.gist: Hadith books open with this because why you act matters to you and to Allah; the names remind you in whose name you act.

outline.heading: Recap of verses 19-21 and recitation of 22
outline.gist: Forget Allah and you forget yourself; the mountain would be humbled by the Quran.

outline.heading: Huwa does not mean male
outline.gist: Arabic uses huwa for any conscious being not purely female; gender does not apply to Allah, and calling Him 'it' would be rude.

outline.heading: No god but He: negation first
outline.gist: Only the Quranic description of God survives philosophical scrutiny; atheists already have the negation half.

outline.heading: A visiting priest's description of God
outline.gist: A priest attending as coursework described God in humanlike terms that shocked him, showing how unique the Muslim conception is.

outline.heading: Tawhid as Islam in one word
outline.gist: Nothing in being Muslim outranks monotheism.

outline.heading: Tawhid is the source of constant values
outline.gist: It is about you, not Allah: values you set yourself or inherit from dead humans keep moving, and moving lines mean nothing.

outline.heading: From 1923 to 2023: values that shift
outline.gist: Western norms changed dramatically, some for the better, because committees, persons or many gods can always be overruled.

outline.heading: A Muslim's values hold anywhere in time
outline.gist: Drop a Muslim in any era or on Mars and he must still be compassionate, fair and honest, rich or poor.

outline.heading: Sinning while knowing is fixable; changing the value is not
outline.gist: Someone who drinks but knows it is haram can be reached; someone who decided it is not has no common ground.

outline.heading: Lines drawn by One who anticipated everything
outline.gist: Allah accounted for your circumstances, so His red lines are permanent even when you lose sight of them.

outline.heading: Knower of the unseen and the seen
outline.gist: Shahadah is all that can be measured; the ghayb, like jinn, cannot be detected by any instrument.

outline.heading: Science can never prove God
outline.gist: Anything science proves is inside time and space and therefore not God; demanding it is a complex-question fallacy.

outline.heading: Live by the seen, take the unseen from revelation
outline.gist: Base decisions on the measurable world and do not go hunting the unseen beyond what the Quran tells.

outline.heading: Al-Rahman: a name Quraysh had never heard
outline.gist: The derivation was newly coined; it denotes unspecified compassion for everything, believers or not.

outline.heading: Al-Rahim: compassion He chooses to give
outline.gist: Rahman is innate and universal, Rahim specific to those He loves; He paired mercy with mercy instead of balancing it with severity.

outline.heading: Without omniscience there is no God
outline.gist: A being who can be surprised can be beaten; every detail of Allah in the Quran is the only possible answer.

outline.heading: Reciting verse 23
outline.gist: The statement of tawhid is repeated to make it clear.

outline.heading: Al-Malik: we are owned
outline.gist: Body and consciousness belong to Allah, so by definition He cannot oppress us.

outline.heading: Rights granted out of grace
outline.gist: No one forced Allah to promise justice; He gave us rights out of His own mercy.

outline.heading: Everyone answers to the King
outline.gist: Whatever people do happens in His kingdom and they will answer for it, which brings serenity and reminds us of our own role.

outline.heading: Al-Quddus: a King without flaws
outline.gist: Human kings fail at a role they were never designed for; no imperfection we can imagine applies to Him.

outline.heading: Pain is part of the story
outline.gist: We only understand things through their opposites, as sweetness through sourness and health through disease, which is why suffering exists.

outline.heading: Al-Salam: free of all harm, granter of peace
outline.gist: The King is not about war or tyranny.

outline.heading: Al-Mu'min and al-Muhaymin
outline.gist: He grants safety and security, and He controls and is fully aware of all that happens in His kingdom.

outline.heading: What I want carries no weight in what happens
outline.gist: Events are part of a destiny He wrote; occupying yourself with what you do not control is out of place.

outline.heading: Al-Aziz: answers to no one

60:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ تُلۡقُونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَقَدۡ كَفَرُواْ بِمَا جَآءَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ يُخۡرِجُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمۡ أَن تُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ رَبِّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ خَرَجۡتُمۡ جِهَٰدࣰ ا فِي سَبِيلِي وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِيۚ تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا۠ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَآ أَخۡفَيۡتُمۡ وَمَآ أَعۡلَنتُمۡۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡهُ مِنكُمۡ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
60:1.en: O ye who believe! Choose not My enemy and your enemy for allies. Do ye give them friendship when they disbelieve in that truth which hath come unto you, driving out the messenger and you because ye believe in Allah, your Lord? If ye have come forth to strive in My way and seeking My good pleasure, (show them not friendship). Do ye show friendship unto them in secret, when I am Best Aware of what ye hide and what ye proclaim? And whosoever doeth it among you, he verily hath strayed from the right way

60:2.ar: إِن يَثۡقَفُوكُمۡ يَكُونُواْ لَكُمۡ أَعۡدَآءࣰ وَيَبۡسُطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡكُمۡ أَيۡدِيَهُمۡ وَأَلۡسِنَتَهُم بِٱلسُّوٓءِ وَوَدُّواْ لَوۡ تَكۡفُرُونَ
60:2.en: If they have the upper hand of you, they will be your foes, and will stretch out their hands and their tongues toward you with evil (intent), and they long for you to disbelieve

60:3.ar: لَن تَنفَعَكُمۡ أَرۡحَامُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُكُمۡۚ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يَفۡصِلُ بَيۡنَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
60:3.en: Your ties of kindred and your children will avail you naught upon the Day of Resurrection. He will part you. Allah is Seer of what ye do

3:119.en: Lo! ye are those who love them though they love you not, and ye believe in all the Scripture. When they fall in with you they say: We believe; but when they go apart they bite their finger-tips at you, for rage. Say: Perish in your rage! Lo! Allah is Aware of what is hidden in (your) breasts

7:150.ar: وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَٰنَ أَسِفࣰ ا قَالَ بِئۡسَمَا خَلَفۡتُمُونِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِيٓۖ أَعَجِلۡتُمۡ أَمۡرَ رَبِّكُمۡۖ وَأَلۡقَى ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأۡسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُۥٓ إِلَيۡهِۚ قَالَ ٱبۡنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱسۡتَضۡعَفُونِي وَكَادُواْ يَقۡتُلُونَنِي فَلَا تُشۡمِتۡ بِيَ ٱلۡأَعۡدَآءَ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡنِي مَعَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
7:150.en: And when Moses returned unto his people, angry and grieved, he said: Evil is that (course) which ye took after I had left you. Would ye hasten on the judgment of your Lord? And he cast down the tablets, and he seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. He said: Son of my mother! Lo! the folk did judge me weak and almost killed me. Oh, make not mine enemies to triumph over me and place me not among the evil-doers

21:87.ar: وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبࣰ ا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقۡدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

06647WYd6pM.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Mumtahinah, Part 1: Verses 1-3
06647WYd6pM.one_line: The story of Hatib's letter and Al-Mumtahinah 1-3: the Muslim baseline is compassion, and Allah had to argue them out of loving enemies who expelled them.
06647WYd6pM.summary: He places Al-Mumtahinah in the Medinan cluster on organising Muslim relationships, here with non-Muslims, combative and non-combative. His key reading principle: the Quran's baseline for Muslims is love and compassion, and its restrictions mark exceptions. He narrates the background: Quraysh's allies massacred Khuza'ah, the Prophet secretly prepared for Mecca, and Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah sent a warning letter to protect his family. The Prophet pardoned him for his stand at Badr, which leads to a lesson: find one hard deed for the ummah that you can bring to Allah, as Musa's stand before Pharaoh outweighed his anger. Verse 1 distinguishes personal enemies from enemies of the nation, defined as those who deny Muslims' right to their faith, lives and land. Allah has to argue at length, in plural address, that Muslims should not throw their love at people who expelled them, which shows how compassionate the companions were. He laments that after 2001 Muslims themselves absorbed the image of a bloodthirsty faith and became uneasy with this surah and with Surat At-Tawbah. Verses 2-3 add that such enemies wish you would lose your faith and that kinship will not help on Judgment Day. The Prophet's prayers for his persecutors at Uhud and at the conquest of Mecca show the mentality he taught.

outline.heading: The Medinan cluster and Al-Mumtahinah's place in it
outline.gist: Previous surahs organised relations among Muslims and citizens; this one covers relations with non-Muslims, combative, non-combative and converts.

outline.heading: The Quran's baseline is compassion; restrictions mark exceptions
outline.gist: Because love is the norm, the Quran repeatedly tells Muslims where not to extend it, so they do not harm themselves.

outline.heading: Conquest of Mecca: Quraysh break the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
outline.gist: Banu Bakr massacred Khuza'ah with Quraysh's blessing, and Abu Sufyan failed to get the treaty renewed in Medina.

outline.heading: Conquest of Mecca: the news arrives and the Prophet plans in secret
outline.gist: A survivor reached Medina with a poem describing the massacre; the Prophet kept his plans hidden and spread word of another destination.

outline.heading: Hatib's letter intercepted
outline.gist: Hatib sent a warning to Quraysh with a woman; Jibril informed the Prophet, and companions retrieved it from her hair.

outline.heading: Hatib explains himself
outline.gist: As an ally without a tribe in Mecca, he feared for his family and believed the outcome would not change.

outline.heading: Umar's anger and the pardon of the people of Badr
outline.gist: The Prophet stopped Umar: Allah may have told the people of Badr to do as they wish, for they are forgiven.

outline.heading: Musa and Yunus: one great deed outweighs mistakes
outline.gist: Musa threw the tablets and seized his brother without rebuke because he had stood before Pharaoh; Yunus, who had not, was punished for leaving his people.

outline.heading: Find the burden you will carry for the ummah
outline.gist: Seek one hard deed that benefits others, which you can bring to Allah despite your shortcomings.

outline.heading: Interlude
'My enemy and yours': personal versus national enemies
outline.gist: The verse is not about personal disputes but about enemies of the Muslim nation.

outline.heading: Who counts as an enemy
outline.gist: Those who deny Muslims' freedom of religion and speech, the sanctity of their lives and their homes, on a national scale; disputes within a country go through the law.

outline.heading: Do not take them as allies
outline.gist: Do not seek alliances or support from those openly bent on removing Muslims, as Quraysh and the Confederates were.

outline.heading: Why such an obvious command was needed
outline.gist: The command only makes sense if Muslims by default extend their hand to everyone.

outline.heading: Throwing your love at those who drop it
outline.gist: The image of love offered and left on the ground; enemies who say they are with you and bite their fingers in rage when alone.

outline.heading: Expelled only for believing in Allah
outline.gist: Allah argues the case: they drove out the Prophet and the believers simply for their faith.

outline.heading: Plural address: the whole community was over-compassionate
outline.gist: The verse speaks to all Muslims because the Prophet taught them to hope for others' guidance and never give up on dawah.

outline.heading: A compassion that needed reining in
outline.gist: Only an excess of compassion explains needing to be told not to befriend those who expelled you.

outline.heading: 'If you went out striving in My path'
outline.gist: Allah brings the weight of His pleasure to persuade them; the verse withholds love and alliance, not more.

outline.heading: The same boundary in personal life
outline.gist: People who deny your right to be your own person should not be showered with love; knowing where to draw a line is protection.

outline.heading: Secret affection and passing on information
outline.gist: Publicly they called Quraysh enemies but inwardly hoped for them; also read as leaking secrets out of love, which is straying from the path.

outline.heading: After 2001 Muslims believed the propaganda
outline.gist: The real loss was Muslims coming to think their faith bloodthirsty and becoming uneasy with words like jihad.

outline.heading: Unease with this surah in the community
outline.gist: This series is always the least attended; people fear what will be said about Muslims and non-Muslims.

outline.heading: Asked not to teach Surat At-Tawbah
outline.gist: At-Tawbah, read in context, urges compassion toward repeated betrayers while drawing a line to stop bloodshed.

outline.heading: No political text speaks of sworn enemies this way
outline.gist: The verse asks only that love and alliance be withheld; he challenges anyone to find comparable restraint in political rhetoric.

outline.heading: A more confident younger generation
outline.gist: Muslims must stop feeling they have to justify themselves; youth are braver and need to be empowered as ambassadors.

outline.heading: Interlude
If they gain the upper hand
outline.gist: An alliance assumes equals; once enemies control you their hostility shows in hands and tongues.

outline.heading: They wish you would lose your faith
outline.gist: The third mention of love in two verses: what they love is your disbelief.

outline.heading: Kinship will not help on Judgment Day
outline.gist: Relatives and children cannot benefit you; Allah separates people by what they did and the rights they allowed others.

outline.heading: Basir: Allah sees outward actions
outline.gist: Allah chose 'All-Seeing', not 'All-Aware', because He forbids visible alliance and affection, not inner goodwill.

outline.heading: Uhud and the well of Badr: the Prophet's mercy toward enemies
outline.gist: Bleeding at Uhud he prayed for his people's forgiveness and guidance; at Badr he spoke to the dead with grief that it had come to this.

outline.heading: What these verses reveal about the companions
outline.gist: He cannot imagine wishing good on those who expelled him, which shows how exceptional their character was.

outline.heading: Conquest of Mecca: 'today is a day of mercy'
outline.gist: The Prophet took the banner from Sa'd ibn Ubadah for calling it a day of slaughter and gave it to his son.

outline.heading: Praying for one of the two Umars
outline.gist: Under persecution he asked Allah to strengthen Islam through one of his fiercest opponents, and one of them accepted.

outline.heading: Of course Muslims wish good for others
outline.gist: That youth ask whether wishing others well is allowed shows the propaganda's damage; Muslims work to benefit everyone.

39:7.ar: إِن تَكۡفُرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنكُمۡۖ وَلَا يَرۡضَىٰ لِعِبَادِهِ ٱلۡكُفۡرَۖ وَإِن تَشۡكُرُواْ يَرۡضَهُ لَكُمۡۗ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةࣱ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
39:7.en: If ye are thankless, yet Allah is Independent of you, though He is not pleased with thanklessness for His bondmen; and if ye are thankful He is pleased therewith for you. No laden soul will bear another's load. Then unto your Lord is your return; and He will tell you what ye used to do. Lo! He knoweth what is in the breasts (of men)

39:8.ar: ۞وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ ضُرࣱّ دَعَا رَبَّهُۥ مُنِيبًا إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلَهُۥ نِعۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡهُ نَسِيَ مَا كَانَ يَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ مِن قَبۡلُ وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا لِّيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦۚ قُلۡ تَمَتَّعۡ بِكُفۡرِكَ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكَ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلنَّارِ
39:8.en: And when some hurt toucheth man, he crieth unto his Lord, turning unto Him (repentant). Then, when He granteth him a boon from Him he forgetteth that for which he cried unto Him before, and setteth up rivals to Allah that he may beguile (men) from his way. Say (O Muhammad, unto such an one): Take pleasure in thy disbelief a while. Lo! thou art of the owners of the Fire

39:9.ar: أَمَّنۡ هُوَ قَٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ سَاجِدࣰ ا وَقَآئِمࣰ ا يَحۡذَرُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ وَيَرۡجُواْ رَحۡمَةَ رَبِّهِۦۗ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
39:9.en: Is he who payeth adoration in the watches of the night, prostrate and standing, bewaring of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, (to be accounted equal with a disbeliever)? Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Are those who know equal with those who know not? But only men of understanding will pay heed

39:10.ar: قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡۚ لِلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣱۗ وَأَرۡضُ ٱللَّهِ وَٰسِعَةٌۗ إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ أَجۡرَهُم بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏

atUTwcun3yQ.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Az-Zumar (39:7-10)
atUTwcun3yQ.one_line: Sincerity as tawhid lived: the gap between belief and practice, forgetting Allah after hardship, the devout night worshipper, and ihsan as being content with His gaze.
atUTwcun3yQ.summary: Az-Zumar treats obedience of the mind through sincerity: tawhid is the value and sincerity its application. Everyone says there is no god but Allah, yet our deeds are not sincere because the self sits in the gap between the idea and its practice, refusing to give up its share; tazkiyah is the lifelong walk of moving tawhid from the tongue into the heart, and sincerity itself is a gift Allah grants to those on that path. Allah does not approve ingratitude for His servants because He holds them in high regard. Verse 8 describes the person who calls on Allah sincerely in distress and then forgets once blessed, setting up rivals in his heart; the root problem is forgetting favours, which the Prophet never did, and the hadith of the last man out of Hell shows how quickly we ask for more. Verse 9 contrasts him with one devoutly obedient through the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy; Muslims today are too comfortable about the Hereafter, unlike Abu Bakr and Umar. Verse 10 commands taqwa, promises good even in this world, reminds that Allah's earth is wide, and grants the patient reward without reckoning, because they reckoned with themselves. Ihsan is being content that Allah sees you; showing off is needing other eyes.

outline.heading: Every surah has its own angle
outline.gist: No surah is less useful; one may move you more because it speaks to your own struggle.

outline.heading: Tawhid is the value, sincerity its application
outline.gist: As justice applies truth, sincerity applies tawhid; Az-Zumar explores sincerity from every side.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah turns an idea into an inner value
outline.gist: Accepting an idea is different from making it real in behaviour; what fills the gap between them?

outline.heading: The self sits in the gap
outline.gist: When no one forces you, the commanding self blocks sincerity because sincere deeds leave it no share.

outline.heading: 'You alone we worship' and the hadith qudsi
outline.gist: Allah says this verse is between Him and His servant: say what you like, the Day will show the truth.

outline.heading: No end to nearness; sincerity is a gift
outline.gist: Unlike physics, there is no final point of closeness to Allah; you walk the path and He grants sincerity to those walking it.

outline.heading: Allah presented Himself so we would be sincere
outline.gist: The previous verses listed His creation and blessings: who else deserves your focus?

outline.heading: Verse 8 recited
outline.gist: The person who calls on Allah in distress and forgets Him in ease.

outline.heading: He does not approve ingratitude for His servants
outline.gist: Kufr here is ingratitude; Allah does not want it for you because you are too honoured for it, as Sheikh Mustafa used to repeat.

outline.heading: Turning away from the One facing you
outline.gist: Allah faces the praying servant and turns away when he turns to something else.

outline.heading: Most sincere in distress
outline.gist: The slightest touch of harm makes people call on Allah alone; then once He grants a favour freely, they forget.

outline.heading: Rivals: treating anything as only Allah deserves
outline.gist: A 'nidd' is anyone or anything treated as only Allah should be, whether or not one claims it is His partner.

outline.heading: Enjoy your ingratitude a little
outline.gist: This is the human pattern with sincerity: sincere in need, slack in ease.

outline.heading: We remember favours we give, not ones we receive
outline.gist: Forgetting hardship is a mercy, but forgetting favours is the self's evasion; the Prophet always recalled others' kindness and never his own.

outline.heading: Never forget what Allah has given
outline.gist: Constant remembrance of His favours makes shirk impossible; we are judged not for forgetting but for not striving to remember.

outline.heading: His promise on release from detention
outline.gist: On release he told Allah he would ask for nothing more, yet within a month the self was asking again.

outline.heading: The last man out of the Fire
outline.gist: He promises to ask nothing more, then asks for tree after tree until Paradise, and is given ten times a great kingdom.

outline.heading: Remember His favour from the womb onward
outline.gist: Parents are the means He used; losing one luxury after years of blessings makes people ungrateful in their hearts.

outline.heading: Verse 9 recited: is he like the devout one?
outline.gist: The omitted half of the question contrasts the ingrate with the night worshipper; a reading with 'amman' noted.

outline.heading: Qunut means sincere devotion
outline.gist: Devoutly obedient wives in An-Nisa are sincere because Allah commanded it; the night worshipper is sincere in hours when no one wants to worship.

outline.heading: Fearing the Hereafter, hoping for mercy
outline.gist: A series of 'Say' commands begins; one who knows does not equal one who does not.

outline.heading: Prostrating and standing: ritual and action
outline.gist: Prostration points to ritual worship and standing to fulfilling one's role in life, as the youths of the cave stood firm.

outline.heading: Muslims are too comfortable about the Hereafter
outline.gist: Abu Bakr wept at death and Umar wished his mother had not borne him; no righteous person died feeling secure.

outline.heading: The believer fears the Day because he understands it
outline.gist: The Prophet prayed until his feet swelled; disbelievers see the Day as far, while believers see it near; only people of understanding remember.

outline.heading: Verse 10: 'O My servants' and the dropped ya
outline.gist: Stopping on 'ibad' is a poor stop; people of understanding remember while others forget, or their hearts die.

outline.heading: Taqwa solves most problems
outline.gist: Taqwa is acting now to shield yourself from bad outcomes before they come.

outline.heading: Ihsan: a relationship unlike any other
outline.gist: We cannot manage even relationships we see and hear; the one with Allah needs special effort to reach worship as if you see Him.

outline.heading: Sincerity is being content with His gaze
outline.gist: Like a child calling 'watch me', we want to be seen; sincerity is content that Allah sees, and showing off is needing other eyes.

outline.heading: Good in this world, and Allah's earth is wide
outline.gist: Allah promises good here too; do not attach your heart to anyone, move on if you must.

outline.heading: The patient rewarded without reckoning
outline.gist: Sincerity is costly; those who reckoned with themselves in this life take a fast lane past the reckoning.

outline.heading: No one enters the Fire feeling wronged
outline.gist: Unlike every prisoner on earth, everyone will admit their deeds did not merit Paradise.

outline.heading: How you treat those who can give you nothing
outline.gist: Your true self shows with people who can offer you nothing; if Allah's eye is enough, you treat everyone alike.

outline.heading: Each surah has its own flavour
outline.gist: Az-Zumar is a demanding matter of the heart, unlike the stories of Sad and As-Saffat.

gVH7V7bqIMw.title: Strength in Unity
gVH7V7bqIMw.one_line: Forty days into the Gaza war, he says the world has been unmasked and calls Western Muslims to unity, never to forget, and justice over comfort.
gVH7V7bqIMw.summary: He opens with the verse about the buried baby girl asked for what sin she was killed, then welcomes the conviction in the murder of London's Afzaal family as a small step toward justice that cannot undo grief, while 11,000 in Gaza still wait for theirs. The forty days of war have unmasked a world governed by power, wealth and narrative rather than justice. Muslims in Canada now celebrate merely getting a representative to ask for a ceasefire, which shows how low the bar is and how little their voice counts. These realizations are not for complaining but for knowing the starting point, since you cannot change what you do not understand, and they must not fade within the usual two weeks. From Al-Anfal he shows that Allah, not wealth, united the believers' hearts, and that strength was never in numbers, as the near-defeat at Hunayn showed. Unity across the community's many nationalities must be the first priority, standing with the oppressed whoever they are. He warns that red lines such as hospitals are being normalized for lack of advocacy. Finally, the hadith of Muslims as froth explains the weakness: love of this world and dislike of death become a disease when comfort outweighs justice, and no injustice, not even a stolen miswak, may be ignored.

outline.gist: Raiding hospitals over a fanny pack and a laptop and bombing evacuated people would never be accepted if the targets hid in the attackers' own country.

outline.heading: Two weeks to forget
outline.gist: Society's memory lasts about two weeks, but what these forty days revealed must be held on to for the rest of our lives.

outline.heading: Power, not justice, governs the world
outline.gist: Strength, politics and wealth let you dictate the narrative however unjust it is; pointing this out from the minbar without making people feel worse is hard.

outline.heading: How low the bar is
outline.gist: Getting a representative merely to ask for a ceasefire is celebrated, though asking will stop nothing; that shows what worth the community actually carries.

outline.heading: Know where you stand in order to change it
outline.gist: When it matters your voice is not equal, while others call people animals or suggest nuking them; these realizations are not for complaining but for knowing your starting point, since you cannot change what you do not understand.

outline.heading: Never fooled again
outline.gist: Those who preached inclusivity and tolerance could not say even "stop killing children"; now we must decide what to advocate for and how much wealth, time and expertise to dedicate.

outline.heading: Masajid must keep speaking about what matters
outline.gist: He has seen places where the minbar talks only of wudu; that voice can be lost, and priorities demand addressing what is relevant.

outline.heading: Emotions pass; we need a long-term plan
outline.gist: The real questions are how to prevent a repeat and influence how the world sees events, and no one yet has the perfect answer.

outline.heading: Allah united their hearts
outline.gist: Al-Anfal: Allah strengthened the Prophet with the believers and joined their hearts, which all the wealth on earth could not have done.

outline.heading: From one-to-ten to one-to-two
outline.gist: Strong believers could face ten times their number; the ratio was eased to two because weakness appeared, and that weakness is a lack of togetherness.

outline.heading: Hunayn: strength was never in numbers
outline.gist: At Hunayn their numbers impressed them and they nearly lost, the wide earth feeling narrow; it has always been unity, so set aside the differences that divide us.

outline.heading: Unity is the first priority
outline.gist: The duty of Muslims in the West is to make their voice reach policymakers, which requires uniting the more than 25 nationalities in this room.

outline.heading: Always on the side of the oppressed
outline.gist: Islam stands with the oppressed, Muslim or not, even against a Muslim oppressor; start with the cause closest to home, but see every injustice as the whole nation's responsibility.

outline.heading: The normalization of crossed red lines
outline.gist: His biggest fear: once a line is crossed without consequence it becomes precedent, while the world schedules another meeting in two weeks.

outline.heading: If hospitals are not safe, what is left?
outline.gist: Hospitals were a red line until a video of a backpack and a laptop made bombing them acceptable; without advocacy and unity the line is nudged until no space remains, and no political pressure yet holds anyone accountable.

outline.heading: They had names
outline.gist: Do not go on as if this never happened; millions of Muslims killed over decades had families and dreams and are not numbers on a poster.

outline.heading: Many, but froth on the flood
outline.gist: The hadith of nations descending on the Muslims like diners on a dish: not because they are few, but because they are weightless froth afflicted by wahn.

outline.heading: Wahn: when comfort outweighs justice
outline.gist: Loving the life Allah gave and disliking death are not wrong, and building a comfortable home is an obligation; the disease is when comfort becomes worth more than justice, truth and integrity.

outline.heading: Not even a stolen miswak
outline.gist: Oppression leaves a darkness on victims, witnesses, oppressors and generations until justice is served, so no injustice may be ignored, even a twig of miswak; our part is to turn our lives around so it is less likely to happen again.

outline.heading: Outro
